items.title: Create Account

reading: Only the SMB brute force (T1110) raised an alert: rule 60204, level 10. The Nmap scan went unseen because the HIDS reads OS logs and Windows Firewall logging was off.
legendCaption: Columns are MITRE ATT&CK tactics. An open eye means detected, a slashed eye not detected, a crossed eye the test did not run, a dashed outline not applicable.

telemetry.heading: SMB brute force (T1110)
telemetry.body: Eight NetExec attempts produced 13 authentication-failure alerts (Event ID 4625), correlated by default rule 60204 at level 10.

telemetry.heading: Nmap scan, T1082, T1547.001
telemetry.body: The agent reads standard OS event logs only, Windows Firewall logging was off and Sysmon was not installed, so the Nmap scan left nothing to alert on. System information discovery (T1082) and the registry Run key (T1547.001) were not caught by the default ruleset.

telemetry.heading: Execution, credential access, defense evasion
telemetry.body: T1059.001, T1003.001 and T1070.001 never ran, so they say nothing about detection. An external payload was missing for the Mimikatz test, ProcDump was unavailable for the LSASS dump, and the log-clearing test was not in the Atomic Red Team version used. These are gaps in my test setup, kept apart from true negatives.

telemetry.heading: Create Account (T1136.001)
telemetry.body: The Atomic Red Team library had no Windows tests for this technique.
